subject: smartphone battery
title: What If You Always Kept Your Phone at 100%?

scenes.text: What if your phone never dropped below 100 percent? It would die sooner, not later.
Phone batteries are lithium ion. Every charge cycle wears them a little.
But sitting full is its own stress. A full cell holds its highest voltage, and that speeds up the chemistry that eats capacity.
In lab tests, a battery kept full at room temperature lost about a fifth of its capacity in a year. Kept at 40 percent, it lost four percent.
Heat makes it worse. Full and hot, the loss roughly doubled.
That's why phones now pause at 80 percent overnight. The last fifth of the tank costs the most.

description:
What if you always kept your phone at 100%? Lithium-ion batteries age faster when they sit at a high state of charge, especially when warm.
Battery University's storage tests: about 80% capacity left after a year at full charge and 25 degrees C, versus 96% at 40% charge; at 40 degrees C and full charge, about 65%. Apple's Optimized Battery Charging holds at 80% to reduce this.
